11920-slave-narratives-a-folk-history-of.title: Slave Narratives A Folk History Of Slavery In The United Sta
11920-slave-narratives-a-folk-history-of.creator: Unknown
11920-slave-narratives-a-folk-history-of.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Uncle Dan tells me "he was born May 5, 1858 at the Abe Wheeler place near Spoonsville, now known as Nina, about nine miles due east from Lancaster. Mother, whose name was Lucinda Wheeler, belonged to the Wheeler family. My father was a slave of Dan Bogie's, at Kirksville, in Madison County, and I was named for him. My mother's people were born in Garrard County as far as I know.

44228-boat-building-and-boating.title: Boat-Building And Boating
44228-boat-building-and-boating.creator: D. C. Beard
44228-boat-building-and-boating.description: A book by D. C. Beard. The stream which cuts your trail is not always provided with bridges of fallen trees. It may be a river too deep to ford and too wide to be bridged by a chance log. Of course it is a simple matter to swim, but the weather may be cold and the water still colder; besides this, you will probably be encumbered with a lot of camp equipage--your gun, rod, and camera--none of which will be improved by a plunge in the water.

arxiv-2110-02579.title: Anomaly Detection based on Compressed Data: an Information Theoretic Characterization
arxiv-2110-02579.creator: Alex Marchioni, Andriy Enttsel, Mauro Mangia, Riccardo Rovatti, and Gianluca Setti
arxiv-2110-02579.description: Abstract We analyze the effect of lossy compression in the processing of sensor signals that must be used to detect anomalous events in the system under observation. The intuitive relationship between the quality loss at higher compression and the possibility of distinguishing anomalous behaviours from normal ones is formalized in terms of information-theoretic quantities.

arxiv-2402-07415.title: Context-aware Multi-Model Object Detection for Diversely Heterogeneous Compute Systems
arxiv-2402-07415.creator: Justin Davis, Mehmet E. Belviranli
arxiv-2402-07415.description: Abstract In recent years, deep neural networks (DNNs) have gained widespread adoption for continuous mobile object detection (OD) tasks, particularly in autonomous systems. However, a prevalent issue in their deployment is the one-size-fits-all approach, where a single DNN is used, resulting in inefficient utilization of computational resources.

arxiv-2409-10782.title: Lattice Light Shift Evaluations In a Dual-Ensemble Yb Optical Lattice Clock
arxiv-2409-10782.creator: Tobias Bothwell 1,* , Benjamin D. Hunt 1,2,* , Jacob L. Siegel 1,2,* , Youssef S. Hassan 1,2 , Tanner Grogan 1,2 , Takumi Kobayashi 1,4 , Kurt Gibble 1,5 , Sergey G. Porsev 6 , Marianna S. Safronova 6 , Roger C. Brown 1 , Kyle Beloy 1 , Andrew D. Ludlow 1,2,3, † \dagger
arxiv-2409-10782.description: Abstract In state-of-the-art optical lattice clocks, beyond-electric-dipole polarizability terms lead to a break-down of magic wavelength trapping. In this Letter, we report a novel approach to evaluate lattice light shifts, specifically addressing recent discrepancies in the atomic multipolarizability term between experimental techniques and theoretical calculations.

arxiv-2410-16584.title: Instanton Floer homology and Milnor fibers Thanks: The first author was partially supported by the Simons Investigator Award-HMS (PI Ludmil Katzarkov) and the University of Miami. The third author was partially supported by the NSF Grant DMS-1952762
arxiv-2410-16584.creator: Kyoung-Seog Lee, Anatoly Libgober, Nikolai Saveliev
arxiv-2410-16584.description: Abstract . In the early days of the Floer theory, Atiyah asked if there is a Milnor fiber description of the Floer homology of the links of singularities. We answer this question for the Brieskorn–Hamm complete intersection singularities. The resulting combinatorial formulas lead to an independent proof of the equality of the Casson invariants in the Donaldson and Seiberg–Witten theories.

arxiv-2410-20017.title: Off-Policy Selection for Initiating Human-Centric Experimental Design
arxiv-2410-20017.creator: Ge Gao, Xi Yang, Qitong Gao, Song Ju, Miroslav Pajic, Min Chi
arxiv-2410-20017.description: Abstract In human-centric tasks such as healthcare and education, the heterogeneity among patients and students necessitates personalized treatments and instructional interventions. While reinforcement learning (RL) has been utilized in those tasks, off-policy selection (OPS) is pivotal to close the loop by offline evaluating and selecting policies without online interactions, yet current OPS methods often overlook the heterogeneity among participants.

arxiv-2507-07352.title: Machine Learning-driven Multiscale MD Workflows: The Mini-MuMMI Experience
arxiv-2507-07352.creator: Loïc Pottier, Konstantia Georgouli, Timothy S. Carpenter, Fikret Aydin, Jeremy O. B. Tempkin, Dwight V. Nissley, Frederick H. Streitz, Thomas R. W. Scogland, Peer-Timo Bremer, Felice C. Lightstone, Helgi I. Ingólfsson
arxiv-2507-07352.description: Abstract Computational models have become one of the prevalent methods to model complex phenomena. To accurately model complex interactions, such as detailed biomolecular interactions, scientists often rely on multiscale models comprised of several internal models operating at difference scales, ranging from microscopic to macroscopic length and time scales.

arxiv-2507-15988.title: High-dimensional graphs convolution for quantum walks photonic applications
arxiv-2507-15988.creator: Roman Abramov, Leonid Fedichkin, Dmitry Tsarev, Alexander Alodjants
arxiv-2507-15988.description: Abstract Quantum random walks represent a powerful tool for the implementation of various quantum algorithms. We consider a convolution problem for the graphs which provide quantum and classical random walks. We suggest a new method for lattices and hypercycle convolution that preserves quantum walk dynamics.

The framework integrates a supervisor model for strategic oversight and a conversational model for question generation. pmc-10672271.title: The Impact of Neck Cooling on Serum Oxidant/Antioxidant Status and HSP70 Levels during High-Intensity Cycling
pmc-10672271.creator: Kyung-Su Choi, Hee-Tae Roh, Su-Youn Cho
pmc-10672271.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Numerous studies have been conducted in an attempt to discover cooling strategies that can be effective in improving exercise performance. However, the mechanism by which neck cooling relieves exercise-induced physiological stress and the optimal cooling temperature are unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effects of neck cooling at different temperatures during high-intensity cycling on body temperature, physiological variables, oxidant/antioxidant status, heat shock protein (HSP) 70 levels, and exercise performance in adolescent athletes.

pmc-10751495.title: Ruptured breast implant removal because of patient anxiety in the absence of breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma
pmc-10751495.creator: Hitomi Takahashi, Hideyoshi Sato, Yukiyo Tsunekawa, Urara Fujioka, Yumi Wanifuchi-Endo, Tatsuya Toyama, Kazuhiro Toriyama
pmc-10751495.description: Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) has been regarded as a long-term problem after silicone breast implantations. We report a case in which BIA-ALCL and breast cancer were not detected preoperatively, with subsequent removal of a ruptured breast implant. A 52-year-old woman had silicone breast implants on both sides for breast augmentation 15 years ago.

pmc-11613969.title: Purification of mitochondria from skeletal muscle tissue for transcriptomic analyses reveals localization of nuclear‐encoded noncoding RNAs
pmc-11613969.creator: Jessica Silver, Adam J. Trewin, Stella Loke, Larry Croft, Mark Ziemann, Megan Soria, Hayley Dillon, Søren Nielsen, Séverine Lamon, Glenn D. Wadley
pmc-11613969.description: Mitochondria are central to cellular function, particularly in metabolically active tissues such as skeletal muscle. Nuclear‐encoded RNAs typically localize within the nucleus and cytosol but a small population may also translocate to subcellular compartments such as mitochondria. We aimed to investigate the nuclear‐encoded RNAs that localize within the mitochondria of skeletal muscle cells and tissue.

pmc-11640529.title: Thermal Manipulation During the Embryonic Stage and the Post-Hatch Characteristics of Broiler Chickens
pmc-11640529.creator: Ana Patrícia Alves Leão, Alexandre Vinhas de Souza, Daniella Rabelo Barbosa, Carina Fernanda Gomes da Silva, Renata Ribeiro Alvarenga, Itallo Conrado Sousa de Araújo, Adriano Geraldo, Carla Oliveira Resende, Márcio Gilberto Zangeronimo, Jeffrey Downing
pmc-11640529.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simple SummaryHeat stress negatively affects broiler chicken production, particularly in high-performance breeds. Researchers have shown that performing thermal manipulation during incubation can improve the birds’ thermotolerance and minimize the negative effects of heat. This study evaluated the influence of increasing the temperature to 39 °C for 3, 12, or 24 h in the last phase of incubation on the hatchability, post-hatch performance, metabolism, and behavioral and physiological changes in broiler chickens.

pmc-13010797.title: Hypoalbuminemia as a predictor of mortality in patients with acute cholangitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13010797.creator: Raja Taha Yaseen Khan, Salman Ahsam, Sanjay Kirshan Kumar, Khaiber Khan, Muhammad Talha Kakar, Ali Hyder, Wadana Malik, Muhammed Mubarak, Nasir H Luck
pmc-13010797.description: BACKGROUNDAcute cholangitis is a potentially life-threatening infection of the biliary tract and its mortality rate is between 10%-30%. Early risk stratification is essential for the best possible outcome. Serum albumin, an index of the inflammatory and nutritional state, has been associated with adverse outcome in various acute conditions.

pmc-13030193.title: Highlighting the Role of Mental Fatigue as a Health Risk Factor: A Narrative Review
pmc-13030193.creator: Jesús Díaz-García, Steven R. Bray, Tomás García-Calvo, Luca Bovolon, Marika Berchicci, Christopher Ring
pmc-13030193.description: Mental fatigue is a psychobiological state induced by sustained effortful cognitive efforts during daily life activities. Yet research efforts in exercise science have focused primarily on performance implications for athletes to the point of exclusion of vulnerable populations for which mental fatigue may be a health risk.

pmc-13066976.title: Extracellular vesicle-derived lncRNA-NEAT1 serves as potential biomarker for the early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-13066976.creator: Chen Li, Qiong Wu, Han Hong, Li Zhou
pmc-13066976.description: BackgroundHepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) ranks as the fourth leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally. Studies have confirmed that long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) derived from extracellular vesicles (EVs) have great potential in the early diagnosis of HCC. LncRNA nuclear enriched abundant transcript 1 (NEAT1) has been shown to be dysregulated in HCC; however, the expression level of EV-derived NEAT1 remains unclear.

pmc-13104791.title: Safety and Efficacy of cceAAV-aflibercept-Fc-YTE (F-CRG-B191): A Gene Therapy for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration
pmc-13104791.creator: Jiemei Shi, Huan Xu, Hongmei Zhao, Jiajie Zhao, Lihui Chen, Ping Xu, Dan Jia, Chunhui Jiang
pmc-13104791.description: PurposeTo evaluate the safety and efficacy of a novel gene therapy vector, covalently closed-end double-stranded adeno-associated virus-aflibercept-Fc-YTE (cceAAV-aflibercept-Fc-YTE; clinical trial name F-CRG-B191), designed for sustained anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression in the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).MethodsWe developed cceAAV-aflibercept-Fc-YTE.

pmc-13124995.title: Glymphatic dysfunction across sleep disorders: a meta-analysis of DTI-ALPS studies
pmc-13124995.creator: Xiaoxin Zhang, Dongmei He
pmc-13124995.description: BackgroundSleep disorders are increasingly linked to glymphatic dysfunction, but whether this impairment is universal across different sleep pathologies remains unclear.ObjectiveThis meta-analysis examined whether glymphatic dysfunction, assessed via the diffusion tensor imaging analysis along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) index, may represent a shared neural feature across a spectrum of sleep disorders.

pmc-13604736.title: A Bioinspired Soft Manipulator Based on Wave Spring Structure: Design and Control
pmc-13604736.creator: Dongbao Sui, Zongwei Zhang, Tianshuo Wang, Sikai Zhao, Yu Zhang, Xinzui Wang
pmc-13604736.description: Architectured soft structures have unlocked new possibilities for designing continuum manipulators with tailored mechanical performance. This work introduces a bioinspired soft manipulator based on modular wave spring units, leveraging the high elasticity of wave spring structures to enable compliant deformation and axial extensibility of the soft manipulator.
